clue.text: Spider bird

explanation.surface: A creature described as both arachnid and avian.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider snares insects in its web, so it is a catcher of flies; the same compound also names a family of small insect-eating songbirds.

clue.text: Hang about and you'll find it in mysterious lore

indicators.note: mysterious suggests something puzzling and jumbled, so the letters of it and lore are rearranged

explanation.surface: Linger and you will discover something in arcane legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang about is to linger idly, dawdling without purpose.

clue.text: Many a dictator overcomes us with this rod

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that overcomes another sits on top of it, so the earlier pieces come above the word us

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian dictator

explanation.surface: Plenty of tyrants rule over us with a staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcomes' places CADUCE above US in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The caduceus is the winged staff with two snakes carried by Hermes, a herald's wand or rod.

clue.text: Bird dived (American style) after the swimmer

indicators.note: after puts the word for dived behind the swimmer in the answer

parts.note: a turtle is a swimming reptile
in American English the past tense of dive is dove

explanation.surface: A bird plunged in after a creature in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The turtle dove is a small wild pigeon famed for its purring call.

clue.text: Here Roman vessels make spasmodic attacks

parts.note: hic is the Latin word for here, so a Roman would say it
cups are drinking vessels

explanation.surface: Ancient Roman pots here bring on fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' tells you to put 'here' into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiccups are involuntary spasms of the diaphragm, coming in bouts or attacks.

clue.text: A rider has a bit of control with this

definitions.text: A rider has a bit of control with this

parts.words: A rider has a bit of control with this
parts.note: a horse rider steers using a strap fastened to the bit in the horse's mouth; 'bit' reads as 'some' but is the mouthpiece

explanation.definitionFit: The strap attached to the bit lets a horseman steer and check the mount.

clue.text: Odd number

explanation.definitionFit: Singular means peculiar or strange; in grammar the singular is the number denoting one, as opposed to plural.

clue.text: Nine legal points in this case ?

definitions.text: Nine legal points in this case ?

parts.words: Nine legal points in this case ?
parts.note: the saying holds that holding something is nine points of the law, and grammar has a case showing ownership

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'possession is nine points of the law' meets the grammatical case of ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical case expressing ownership, linked to the proverb about holding property.

clue.text: The East thus includes a Kipling character, a Greenlander perhaps

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

indicators.note: includes signals that the word for thus holds the character within it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name

explanation.surface: An Arctic native and a Kipling hero turn up in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit peoples of Greenland were formerly called by this name, so a Greenlander is an example.

clue.text: This ode involves 500 in Capri

indicators.note: involves in its sense of entangling signals that the letters are mixed together

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A poem mentions some number of things on an Italian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' rearranges D, IN and CAPRI together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pindaric ode is one written in the elaborate style of the Greek poet Pindar.

clue.text: Transmits far from favourable omens?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
omens are signs of what is to come

explanation.surface: Sends out portents that are anything but good.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to send or hand them over for delivery.

clue.text: See the Indian creep softly away

indicators.note: away tells you the letter for softly goes from the word creep

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Watch the Native American sneak quietly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'softly' and 'away' read as the creeping, but they take P from CREEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a Native American people of Canada and the northern US.

clue.text: Hoped copal could be extracted from an octopus ?

indicators.note: could be extracted suggests reworking the letters of hoped copal into something new

explanation.surface: A hope that resin might be drawn out of an octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: Copal is a tree resin. The question mark marks the octopus as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is one example of this class of molluscs, alongside squid and cuttlefish.

clue.text: Arnold's hero made dramatically volcanic exit

definitions.text: Arnold's hero made dramatically volcanic exit

parts.words: Arnold's hero made dramatically volcanic exit
parts.note: Matthew Arnold wrote a dramatic poem about the Greek philosopher who is said to have died by leaping into Etna

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold's poem 'Empedocles on Etna' ends with the philosopher throwing himself into the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian philosopher of the four elements, who legend says leapt into Etna, is the subject of Arnold's poem.

clue.text: About one hundred language varieties used in logical discussion

indicators.note: about signals that the language varieties go round the numerals

parts.note: dialects are regional varieties of a language
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Roughly a hundred regional tongues feature in reasoned debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'roughly'; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectics is the art of reasoning by questioning and argument, a method of logical debate.

clue.text: This fruit all the rage ?

explanation.definitionFit: Passion fruit is a tropical fruit; passion is also intense emotion or rage, a sense in 'all the rage'.

clue.text: S African minstrel leader heard in church

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South African

indicators.note: heard tells you the leader's name is taken by its sound and spelt differently

parts.note: E. P. Christy led the Christy Minstrels, a famous American troupe

explanation.surface: A South African troupe director is listened to in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: Many a doctor needs change of air in a French town

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: change of tells you to rearrange the letters of air

explanation.surface: Many doctors need fresh air in a French resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of air' sounds like a health cure; it rearranges AIR to RAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambrai is a town in northern France, site of a First World War battle.

clue.text: Choosing the lead, he won the leading lady

definitions.text: Choosing the lead, he won the leading lady

parts.words: Choosing the lead, he won the leading lady
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the suitor who picks the lead casket wins Portia, the heroine

explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal of the casket in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, not 'leading role'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's suitor chose the lead casket and so won Portia's hand.

clue.text: Such a bind, when one's wounded.

definitions.text: Such a bind, when one's wounded.

parts.words: Such a bind, when one's wounded.
parts.note: 'bind' reads as a nuisance, but means the dressing wrapped round an injury

explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material bound round an injury is a dressing.

clue.text: Champion flier' eats treacle mixture to increase speed

indicators.note: eats tells you the pilot's word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: an ace is a champion fighter pilot

indicators.note: mixture signals that the letters of treacle are jumbled

explanation.surface: A top pilot gobbles a syrupy blend to go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' turns TREACLE into CELERAT, which 'eats' puts inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to go faster, picking up speed.

clue.text: Herbal ingredient in sausages

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the word sausages

explanation.surface: A herb used in making sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an aromatic herb, a classic seasoning in sausages and stuffing.

clue.text: Old Faithful could get you in hot water

definitions.text: Old Faithful could get you in hot water

parts.words: Old Faithful could get you in hot water
parts.note: Old Faithful is a famous hot spring in Yellowstone, and in Britain the same word is a gas water heater

explanation.walkthrough: 'get you in hot water' sounds like trouble, but literally means supplying heated water.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Faithful in Yellowstone is a hot spring that spouts; British homes also had water heaters of the same name.

clue.text: Scientifically burnt

parts.note: to a chemist, burning is combination with oxygen

explanation.definitionFit: Combustion is chemically a reaction with oxygen, so a burnt substance has combined with it.

clue.text: Jerusalem loses nothing, gains carbon element

indicators.note: gains tells you the symbol for carbon is added at the end
loses tells you the letter for nothing drops out of the name

parts.note: Zion is a poetic name for Jerusalem
O is nothing, zero
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: The holy city gives up none and picks up a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes O from ZION, leaving ZIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, number 30.

clue.text: You'd be crazy to see him. For a foreigner it's different

definitions.text: You'd be crazy to see him

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that only the mad would visit a certain man, and the word differs for an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: An alienist is an old word for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: An alienist was a doctor treating mental illness, whom only the insane would need to consult.

clue.text: How debtors get away from the constable ?

definitions.text: How debtors get away from the constable ?

parts.words: How debtors get away from the constable ?
parts.note: the old idiom 'to overrun the constable' means to run into debt, read here literally as escaping the policeman

explanation.walkthrough: To 'outrun the constable' is an old idiom for spending beyond one's means.
explanation.definitionFit: Debtors running up bills beyond their means are said to leave the constable behind.

clue.text: Reykjavik battleground

parts.note: Fischer and Spassky fought the 1972 world championship match in Reykjavik

explanation.walkthrough: The 1972 Fischer-Spassky world chess championship was held in Reykjavik.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkered board was the field of combat in the famous 1972 Reykjavik title match.
